cards.title: Reddit comments as sentiment, not a discovery lever
cards.claim: The speaker says Reddit comments have not been seen to meaningfully change discovery direction and are more for sentiment; commenting alone is not expected to increase citations or move a brand to the top. Negative-sentiment comments can become indexed and hard to remove, and the speaker theorizes LLMs may have a bias toward picking up bad sentiment.
cards.action: Treat Reddit comments primarily as a sentiment channel; do not rely on commenting alone to increase citations or ranking, and avoid negative-sentiment comments that could be indexed.
applies_when: already getting discovered via Reddit or in ChatGPT
considering Reddit comments as a way to increase citations or rank
monitoring brand or product sentiment around Reddit discussions
do_not_use_when: the goal is to prove comment volume causes higher LLM citations
there is no evidence comments affect ranking or discovery
unknowns: Whether comments ever meaningfully change discovery direction
Whether LLMs systematically favor negative sentiment
How long negative indexed sentiment persists or how to remove it reliably
evidence_quotes: I haven't seen comments having a meaningful impact act in changing the direction of your discovery.
I think comments are more for sentiment
if you're thinking that hey I would just keep commenting and I would you know end up being on the top or you know my charge citations would increase I don't think that would work.
bad sentiment you have to avoid at all cost because if there's a bad sentiment LLM have bias towards picking that up

cards.title: Niche down and keep citations always-on
cards.claim: LLM/Reddit citation competition is described as similar to SEO because LLM queries use only a few references, so brands compete against competitors. The speaker suggests reducing competition by targeting narrower queries such as 'best CRM for SMB/fintech/health tech' before trying broad terms, and says the work is an always-on engine because citations may have a half-life.
cards.action: For competitive broad categories, target narrower niche queries first, then attempt broader terms; treat Reddit/LLM citation work as ongoing rather than one-time because citations may decay.
applies_when: LLM/Reddit citations are limited to a few references
building topical authority before targeting broad best-X terms
do_not_use_when: the source's lack of a thesis on LLM ranking factors is treated as proof
a niche query has no relevance or demand
unknowns: What LLMs look at when choosing Reddit citations
Whether a citation half-life exists and how long it is
Whether niche targeting produces citation gains

What is the best CRM for fintech? What is the best CRM for health tech?

cards.title: Open ecosystem positioning and strategic competitor choice
cards.claim: The speaker recommends making a tool open and using open ecosystem/integration features such as MCP, Zapier, and export as a positioning angle. The speaker also advises choosing which competitors to talk about rather than defaulting to all competitors in Reddit/AEO content.
cards.action: If the tool is open, emphasize the open ecosystem and integrations such as MCP, Zapier, and export; choose which competitors to compare against rather than mentioning all of them.
applies_when: the tool actually supports an open ecosystem or integrations
participating in Reddit conversations around CRM or tool ecosystems
deciding which competitors to mention in AEO/Reddit content
do_not_use_when: the tool does not support the claimed open ecosystem or integrations
the goal is to make unverified comparative claims
unknowns: Whether emphasizing openness improves LLM citations
Whether choosing competitors changes citation outcomes
evidence_quotes: make sure that your tool is open
our tool is open ecosystem but can your tool support an open ecosystem
you can always talk about that hey our tool is open right you can use MCP you can connect it to Zapier you can export and so on but hey this XYZ presentation tool doesn't let you do all of that
choose the competitors that you would want to talk about
you can just choose you know who who do you want to place yourself against
